summary.headline: Shakti Pumps Q1 FY27 revenue rose 37.9% YoY to INR859 crores, but EBITDA margin stayed near 9.6% on raw material and realisation pressure.
summary.overview: Management reported a record quarterly revenue of INR859 crores (up 37.9% YoY from INR623 crores) and PAT of INR52 crores, up 35% QoQ, with PAT margin at 6% versus 4.5% in Q4 FY26. EBITDA margin was about 9.6%, which management said was broadly stable sequentially, while YoY EBITDA fell from INR144 crores to INR83 crores due to raw material inflation (about INR36 crores) and lower sales realisation (about INR25 crores). Solar pump installations rose 57.6% YoY to 27,678 units, and the order book was about INR1,000 crores as of 22 July 2026. Management reiterated a target of INR5,000 crores revenue by FY29 and tied margin recovery to PM-KUSUM 2.0 launch and easing raw material prices.

segments.name: Solar pumps (core)
segments.commentary: Installations up 57.6% YoY to 27,678 pumps; order book about INR1,000 crores (B2G, mostly government), management says executable within two quarters. Recent INR350 crore Maharashtra order cited.

segments.name: Solar rooftop
segments.commentary: Revenue INR8 crores vs INR2 crores a year ago. Company registered as brand owner under PM Surya Ghar; 0.5 GW panel plant expected to support integrated offering. Rooftop order book described as negligible.

segments.name: Cash and retail sales
segments.commentary: Sales of INR24 crores in Q1 FY27, described as strong growth, supported by dealer network expansion.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Described as steady; about INR100 crores of export orders received every quarter. Management said the Middle East conflict had not materially affected the business.

segments.name: EV motors
segments.commentary: In trial and validation phase; management expects 6-9 months more before revenue ramp, with meaningful contribution from FY28.

guidance_outlook: Target of becoming an INR5,000 crore company by FY29 (within three years), with no split by business given.
Management expects EBITDA margins to improve gradually QoQ as raw material prices ease and PM-KUSUM 2.0 orders arrive.
Post 2.2 GW integrated cell and module capacity, management expects about 3% EBITDA margin expansion; rooftop plus module integrated target around 15% EBITDA margin.
No EBITDA target given for three years out; company says it will update quarterly.

Order book of INR1,000 crores expected to be executed over the next two quarters, plus new orders from pipeline; management said run rate of last two quarters to be maintained, subject to rain and flood conditions.
Capex of INR1,500-1,700 crores to be completed by September 2027, with about INR800 crores in FY27 and the balance in FY28.
capex_capacity: 0.5 GW DCR solar module plant expected to be completed in September 2026; management said it would run at 40-50% in the first month, 60-70% in the second, then about 85%.
2.2 GW integrated DCR cell and module project targeted for September 2027.
Pump plant capacity expansion slated for November 2026, per management.
Company currently buys about 50-60 MW of solar pump modules externally each month; in-house capacity to replace this over time.

Working capital limits of about INR1,800 crores from about 10 Indian banks and one Qatar bank; term loan of about INR800 crores for the 2.2 GW project. Two QIPs funded equity, including INR200 crores with no bank loan.
demand_pricing: PM-KUSUM 2.0 described as ready for launch and with the PMO; management said it could be announced within weeks. Management expects orders under it to begin by end of the current quarter.
Other states' schemes (MP, Rajasthan) have not yet launched and are expected alongside KUSUM 2.0.
Receivables: about INR760 crores not yet due, about INR560 crores over 180 days, and INR477 crores retention amount. Maharashtra payments have started coming in.
Raw material cost rose about 6% YoY (stainless steel, copper, aluminium, mild steel); management said some inputs softened by INR1-1.5 recently.
Realisation impact of about 4% YoY attributed partly to sales mix across PM-KUSUM and Magel Tyala orders.
Management said no El Nino-driven demand uptick so far; higher-HP pump demand emerging in Haryana and Punjab.
No hedging of raw material prices, as management views the pressure as temporary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of raw material and realisation on margins, and when will they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said YoY EBITDA margin impact was about 10%: about INR36 crores (6%) from raw materials and INR25 crores (4%) from lower realisation. It expects gradual QoQ margin improvement as raw material prices ease and KUSUM 2.0 orders arrive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the business split of the INR5,000 crore FY29 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split revenue by business, saying only that all segments are expected to contribute and that updates will be given quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR1,500-1,700 crores to be completed by September 2027, with about INR800 crores in FY27 and the rest in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company expect to win PM Surya Ghar orders without margin hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not take a margin hit; the segment is B2B with lower margins, and integrated inverters, structures and panels are expected to help it become a leader.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV motors timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The product is in validation and testing for another 6-9 months, with meaningful revenue expected from FY28 onwards.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin remains near 10% versus 24-25% in FY24-25; management has not given a multi-year margin target.
Receivables: INR560 crores over 180 days and INR477 crores retention outstanding; collection timing depends on state nodal agencies.
PM-KUSUM 2.0 launch timing has slipped in messaging, and other state schemes depend on it.
Order book of about INR1,000 crores; management declined to give quarter-wise execution split, and monsoon conditions may affect execution.
Capacity commissioning timelines (0.5 GW in September 2026; 2.2 GW in September 2027) and ramp-up at 40-85% utilisation.
Competitive intensity in tenders and rising raw material prices across the industry; EV revenue timeline remains uncertain.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, volumes and capacity timelines, but cautious and non-committal on margins, EBITDA targets, and segment-wise revenue splits. Management repeatedly framed margin pressure as temporary and external without providing a numerical recovery path.
key_quotes: Our EBITDA margin remained broadly stable on a sequential basis at 9.6%.
we view these margin pressures as temporary and largely external in nature, rather than reflective of any structural issue in the business.
We cannot give an EBITDA target for three years right now. We update it every quarter.

Going forward, with KUSUM 2.0 expected to come in and raw material prices likely to ease as the geopolitical situation stabilizes, we expect margins to improve gradually on a quarter-on-quarter basis.
we are making these investments with the goal of becoming a INR5,000 crores company over the next three years.

adds.what: 2.2 GW integrated DCR cell and module project (capex part of INR1,500-1,700 crore program, about INR800 crore in FY27)

growth.why: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 37.9% YoY to INR859 crore with a ~INR1,000 crore order book, and the company targets INR5,000 crore revenue by FY29 (roughly 100% growth over ~3 years from current run-rate, implying ~80% CAGR from INR3,400 crore annualised), backed by 0.5 GW module plant, pump expansion and INR1,500-1,700 crore capex to Sep 2027; utilisation is only 63%.
